title: AI-Driven Resume Quality & ATS Analysis System
description: Built an agentic resume tailoring system that ingests resume, GitHub, and LinkedIn data into a skills knowledge graph, then orchestrates a pipeline of LLM agents (via LangGraph and Anthropic/OpenAI models) to plan, generate, and iteratively score ATS-optimized one-page resumes against specific job descriptions. The system produces LaTeX-rendered PDF and DOCX outputs, logs every tailoring decision with reward signals for future learning, and exposes a React/FastAPI chat interface where users propose, review, and approve revisions in real time. Deployed to Railway as a single-process full-stack application with a PostgreSQL-backed decision log and a live demo serving end-to-end resume tailoring workflows.

title: Job_Tracker
description: Built an automated job tracking pipeline that scraped and scored early-apply New Grad 2027 and internship postings across six technical tracks (software engineering, data science, machine learning, and AI engineering) using Python with Playwright for browser-based board scraping and PostgreSQL for job storage. The system fetched job descriptions from ~60 Workday boards and aggregated sources, then matched postings against an ingested resume profile using skill-vocabulary scoring to filter roles admitting a Data Science major with a 2027 graduation. Scored results were pushed to a Notion board and delivered via Discord digest with daily pings, while a Windows Scheduled Task automated twice-daily refreshes across the full pipeline.

title: Alongside
description: Alongside was a longitudinal treatment companion for cancer patients that addressed the polypharmacy coordination gap — the failure mode where two doctors each prescribe something individually safe, but no system catches the combined contraindication. The application accumulated daily patient check-ins (typed or voice) into a persistent Jac knowledge graph, where drug interaction constraints were encoded as graph edges rather than vector embeddings, making a mandatory traversal block new substance additions and making missing safety constraints visibly inspectable rather than silently unranked. The graph-based architecture transformed the interaction safety guarantee from a retrieval approximation into a structural property, and surfaced longitudinal symptom patterns as citation-backed questions patients could bring to their next appointment.

title: Portfolio

The site uses vanilla HTML, CSS, and ES modules across four pages — a hero landing page, an experience timeline, a filterable project grid, and a rendered resume — all driven by a single `data/site.js` source-of-truth file. Automated Node.js scripts sync GitHub repository metadata and merge it back into the data layer without overwriting editorial content, keeping project listings current with zero manual duplication.

title: RollAway
description: RollAway was a map-first progressive web app built exclusively for San Francisco mobile food vendors, ranking legal vending locations by scoring setbacks, competition density, travel time, and foot traffic derived from a full year of Bay Wheels trip history and DataSF permit feeds. Hard constraints — including SF Public Works Order 182101 setback rules, SFMTA street closures, and school/hydrant clearances — were enforced deterministically in code, with LLMs used solely to generate cited natural-language explanations grounded in precomputed signals. The app also collapsed SF's four-agency permit process (Public Works, DPH, Fire, Treasurer) into a single guided checklist with real forms, fees, and ordering constraints encoded directly into the application logic.

title: AI Agent Policy Optimization
description: Built a reinforcement learning policy optimizer for an AI-driven HVAC contractor follow-up agent, training a decision engine to select among seven actions (such as CHECK_IN, ESTIMATE_NUDGE, ESCALATE, and SEND_OPT_OUT) based on homeowner conversation state. Implemented a tabular Q-learning approach in pure Python — no external ML dependencies — using a simulated episode environment that modeled realistic homeowner objections, engagement decay, and opt-out risk to generate training signal. The resulting policy balanced conversion rate against customer trust and opt-out risk, outperforming a naive always-nudge baseline by reducing unnecessary contacts while maintaining estimate follow-up effectiveness.

title: Diginetica: GNN vs. Flat Ranker for Session Recommendation
description: Built an end-to-end relational deep learning pipeline on the Diginetica (CIKM Cup 2016) e-commerce logs, using RelBench to convert the relational database into a heterogeneous graph — 8 node types (items, sessions, users plus view/query/click/queried-item/purchase events) and 22 edge types over 11 foreign-key relations. Engineered an `abs_time` event clock at microsecond resolution by folding intra-session millisecond offsets into the event date, enabling time-aware neighbor sampling that admits only neighbors strictly earlier than a per-row seed time so the receptive field never peeks at the future. Defined two tasks: session-conversion entity classification (binary, ~4% positive rate, AUPRC/AUROC) and next-item link prediction via intra-session leave-last-out on 218K sessions. The GNN is a two-tower heterogeneous GraphSAGE encoder (HeteroEncoder + temporal encoder) splitting into session and item towers scored by dot product, trained with sampled-softmax over in-batch and pool negatives. It is compared against an XGBoost LambdaRank ranker (`rank:ndcg`) over anchor-based 1-hop features — co-view, co-purchase, transition, category, popularity, price, is_repeat. A shared per-row candidate pool (co-view + transition + co-purchase + category + popularity backfill, built on train statistics only) lets both models rank the identical set, isolating ranking quality from candidate recall, with Optuna sweeps (persistent SQLite, median pruning) tuning both on Novel Recall@10. Evaluation decomposes Recall@10, NDCG@10, and MRR across slices — Repeat/Novel, popularity (Head/Torso/Tail), and session length — through a single masked `task.evaluate` code path, alongside structural ablations on hop depth, item-feature capacity, and scoring head (pooled dot vs. maxpool vs. ColBERT-style late interaction).

title: Idx_cont_training
description: Built an end-to-end MLOps pipeline for continuously training machine learning models on real estate listing data, leveraging a streaming data architecture to keep models updated as new listings entered the market. Implemented gradient boosting models (LightGBM, XGBoost) with automated preprocessing steps including geospatial feature engineering via GeoPandas, missing value imputation, and outlier detection using custom utility modules. The pipeline integrated scikit-learn workflows with joblib serialization to enable reproducible model versioning and deployment across iterative training cycles.

title: Portfolio Live Editor
description: Built an Express.js proxy server that intercepted live HTTP responses from a personal portfolio site and injected a WYSIWYG editing overlay into every served page, enabling point-and-click content editing directly on the rendered site. The overlay communicated with a custom REST API to read and write changes to a source JSON data file in real time, bypassing any build pipeline or recompilation step. This replaced manual source file edits with an in-place visual interface, eliminating context-switching between the live site and raw data files during content iteration.

title: Real Time ML Feature Store And Quant Research Platform
description: Built a modular quantitative research platform featuring a real-time ML feature store, event-driven backtesting engine, and tax-loss harvesting rules engine, using Python with DuckDB, Apache Arrow/Parquet, and Feast as core infrastructure. The pipeline ingests daily OHLCV data and corporate actions via Yahoo Finance, computes engineered features stored in a Feast feature store, and feeds a mean-reversion classifier that gates tax-loss harvesting decisions. The system was structured across six sequential build phases, integrating wash-sale-aware position tracking, lot-level trade logging, and an ML model trained to identify harvest opportunities within a unified backtesting framework.

title: eCommerce Session Review Analysis - Predicting Online Shopper Purchase Intent
description: Built classification models using Random Forest and XGBoost on 12,330 e-commerce browsing sessions to predict purchase intent, applying threshold tuning to maximize recall and reduce missed conversions, achieving approximately 90% accuracy.
